solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Skip round little boy, jumping up

indicators.note: in a down light, jumping up sends the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: a round shape is the letter O
Tim is a boy's name, and Tiny Tim is the little boy of A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A tubby little lad hops about skipping, or skipping a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little boy goes upward; the round stays at the top of OMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip something is to leave it out or pass over it, the everyday sense of the verb.

clue.text: Article borne by diminutive, climbing, pack animals

indicators.note: something borne is carried inside, so the article sits within the other word
in a down light, climbing means the letters go upward, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: diminutive means small
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Small pack animals carry an item up a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside SMALL to make SAMALL, which is then read upward as LLAMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American beasts of burden used to carry loads in the Andes.

clue.text: I had poor Isolde worshipped

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the name's letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: I had contracts to I'd
the name, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A confession of having adored poor Isolde, the tragic heroine of Tristan and Isolde.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to treat them as an idol, adoring them as one would a god.

clue.text: Cruel old ruler’s verse on youth

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for verse
a youth is a lad

explanation.surface: A poem about a tyrant's early years, as if read by a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay; 'on' puts verse before youth in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Vlad the Impaler was a fifteenth-century Wallachian prince famous for brutality, the model for Dracula.

clue.text: One who’s fled bad regime?

indicators.note: bad means corrupted or spoilt, telling us the next word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A refugee escaping an oppressive government.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a typical exile is fleeing a bad regime.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country, often for political reasons.

clue.text: One turning back from minister and queen twice embracing son

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the pair of royals wraps around the next letter

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a church minister
ER (Elizabeth Regina) written twice
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A clergyman and a queen hugging a boy, oddly pictured as a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The son sits between the two ERs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that reverses turns things back the other way, so it is one turning back.

clue.text: Proceeded casually — risked losing the lead

indicators.note: the lead is the front position, so the word's first letter is dropped

blocks.note: to risk money or safety is to gamble it

explanation.surface: A runner who took a chance, fell behind, and then just strolled on.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the G from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, going along casually.

clue.text: Feeble Hollywood movie: but it’s hard to shake off!

blocks.note: limp means weak or feeble
E.T., Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: A weak Hollywood film that nonetheless sticks in the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A limpet is a shellfish that clings to rocks so tightly it is notoriously difficult to dislodge.

clue.text: Dumbest fool, finally moving, nearly fell

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of that word, so only its closing letter is used
letters that are moving shift out of place into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
the last letter of fool

explanation.surface: An idiot on the move almost took a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip and lose one's footing, coming close to falling over.

clue.text: Got larger plug rewired, partially

indicators.note: partially means only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An electrician's half-finished job on a plug.
explanation.definitionFit: Grew is the past tense of grow, meaning increased in size.

clue.text: State of king meeting an elite army unit

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
taken as written
the SAS is the British Special Air Service

explanation.surface: A monarch's realm receiving a visit from special forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun for condition, but it is the American one.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Unconventional star upset before hit national shows

indicators.note: the words shows the answer by displaying it inside their letters
upset means turned over, and in a down light the letters run upward

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: An offbeat celebrity was put out before a song became a national hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a central character lacking conventional heroic qualities, an unconventional lead.

clue.text: Sporting events: matches?

blocks.note: first meaning: athletics gatherings or race days
second meaning: the verb, equals or corresponds to

explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like another word for sporting events, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A meet is a sports meeting; and if one thing meets another, it equals or satisfies it.

clue.text: Ticks abandon old fly

blocks.note: a tick is a moment, a mo, so ticks are mos
to quit is to abandon
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Parasites leaving an elderly host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ticks' and 'fly' together suggest insects, but the ticks are moments ('in a tick').
explanation.definitionFit: A mosquito is a small two-winged insect, and true flies belong to the order Diptera.

clue.text: I turn on stove in the end

indicators.note: in the end points to the final position of that word, so only its closing letter counts
in an across light, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the turn is written second

blocks.note: the last letter of stove
a turn in a game is a go

explanation.surface: Someone switching on the cooker at last.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across light, 'turn on stove' puts the turn after the stove's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is the self, the sense of 'I' one has as a person.

clue.text: Did DIY in bathroom I’d let out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are let loose and set down again in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone admitting they handed a home-improvement job over to someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting tiles on bathroom walls is a typical home-improvement job, so tiled is one way of doing DIY there.

clue.text: Permissive character?

blocks.note: surface reading: a lax, indulgent person
setter's reading: one who lets things happen, which is also a symbol of the alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: One who lets is a 'letter', and a letter is also a character in writing; the question mark flags the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A character of the alphabet is a letter, and one who permits or lets could be called a letter too.

clue.text: Expedition’s endless voyage, covering a great distance

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut off
covering means going around, so the shortened word wraps the next pieces

blocks.note: a sail is a trip by boat
taken as written
far means a great distance away

explanation.surface: A long trip that seems to go on forever over huge distances.
explanation.walkthrough: The sail loses its L, and SAI then wraps around A and FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, especially in Africa to see or hunt wild animals.

clue.text: Person having stock of bacteria for germ warfare — murder, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so each word gives only its closing letter

blocks.clueFragment: of bacteria for germ warfare — murder
blocks.note: the final letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: A sinister scientist keeping a supply of bacteria for biological weapons and murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests a lab culture of germs, but it means livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer keeps livestock, cattle and sheep, so is a person who has stock in that sense.

clue.text: Try second helping of this? Just starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so only the first letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A diner offered more, asking for only appetisers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starters' looks like part of the meal scene, but it marks the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot is an informal synonym for an attempt, as in 'give it a shot', so it means a try.

clue.text: Singular spicy dishes can give you runs

blocks.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
curries are spicy dishes

explanation.surface: A warning that hot food may upset the stomach, 'the runs' being slang for diarrhoea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb: someone who scurries runs quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to move hurriedly with short quick steps, so scurries means runs.

clue.text: Appear to understand spy chief

blocks.note: 'I see' means I understand
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: An agent who seems to grasp what the boss wants.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give the impression of being something, which is what appear means.

clue.text: Rest of newspaper oddly skipped

indicators.note: oddly points at the odd positions, which are thrown away to leave every second letter
skip can mean leap over, so the kept letters jump back over themselves and run the other way

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The remainder of a paper with some pages missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skipped' reads as part of dropping the odd letters, but it has to reverse them; the blogger and commenters found this a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is relaxation or repose, the state of being at rest.

clue.text: Stop to deliver outside of zone

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its two edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: to deliver someone is to set them free
the first and last letters of zone

explanation.surface: A courier told to halt before dropping off a parcel at the edge of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to become motionless, halting suddenly, as in a police command.

clue.text: Article first put together for believer

blocks.note: the definite article
1st, with the numeral 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: An essay's lead item assembled to make a case for faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often write the digit 1 as I, so 1ST becomes IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is someone who believes in the existence of a god.
